clusters.title: Wording about the beam's own weight is misread: 'does not include beam weight' becomes NEGLECT, 'beam weight not included' and 'its own weight' / 'plus the weight of a W16x26' are not read at all
clusters.root_cause: reader.js neglectSelf() (2093-2101) treats a STATEMENT that the load leaves the weight out as an instruction to neglect it. (1) Alternative 1 'not\s+include' (2094) has no subject check, so 'does not include beam weight' / 'the dead load does not include the weight of the beam' match. (2) The last alternative '\bdead\s+load\b[^.;]{0,24}?\bincluding ...weight' (2100) skips the 'not' in 'dead load of 1 klf not including beam weight' and in '(not including the beam weight)'. selfMentions() correctly gives kind 'not' (= add), but all three users veto on neglectSelf: beamAnalysisFields 2195 (named beam), FILL.beam_select 2279 (self_weight_recheck) and FILL.beam_max_live_load 2320-2322 (include_self_weight=false, high). (3) The bare passive '(beam weight not included)' / 'self wieght not included' (no is/are) is read by neither SELF_PASSIVE_RE (2055 needs is/are) nor neglectSelf (needs a second 'weight'), so the page treats the text as if it never mentioned the weight and asks nothing. (4) addSelf() (2087-2092) does not know 'carries only its own weight' or 'plus the weight of a W16x26'. I confirmed all 10 still fail on cloud 448cad5 and probed the functions on the branch.
clusters.fix_plan: reader.js only, in neglectSelf/addSelf plus one ask. (1) In neglectSelf, after the alt-1 exec, drop the match when 'not include' is a statement: the slice before it ends in does / doesn't / 'doesnot', or in a load subject (load(s)|it|this|that|which|they|these|values) + 'do'. The imperative 'do not include' / 'don't include' at a clause start stays NEGLECT. (2) The last alternative's span may not cross not/without: (?:(?!\bnot\b|\bwithout\b)[^.;]){0,24}?. I prototyped (1)+(2) on a scratch copy and ran all 4,718 corpus questions: 9 change, every one to the right value (178/179/22/33/102/169: 409.73; 31: W21X48; 70: W18X40; 32: 219.4; noise-144: W14X26) and nothing regresses. (3) addSelf, kind add: '\bcarr(?:y|ies)\s+(?:only\s+)?its\s+own\s+weight' and '\b(?:plus|and|in\s+addition\s+to)\s+(?:the\s+|its\s+)?(?:own\s+weight|self[- ]?weight|weight\s+of\s+(?:the\s+|an?\s+)?(?:beam|W\s?\d+\s*[xX]\s*\d+))'. The named-beam rule (2195) then takes the weight from the single shape: ANSWER 121.8 (96) and 111.56 (151). With no single named shape, beam_select uses the existing recheck; otherwise ASK. BC-095 'In addition to its own weight' also reads this way. (4) The bare passive '(?:self|beam|member)[- ]?w(?:ei|ie)ghts?\s+not\s+included' with no is/are has two readings: A2-beam-232 puts the same words after the blank, where they mean 'answer without it'. ASK with kind 'need'. In beam_analysis, ask for self_weight_plf ('type the beam's own weight in lb/ft, or zero if it is to be ignored', no digits in the text). In beam_max_live_load, ask for include_self_weight with the existing yes/no choices, now kind 'need'. This gives ASK for 180 and 231 and never the silent default. MUST NOT CHANGE: 'neglect / ignore / disregard self weight'; the imperative 'do not include the beam weight' (neglect); 'including its own weight' right after a load (has); 'beam weight is not included' (SELF_PASSIVE kind 'not' = add, already 232.53); her Q20 '(Include the self-weight of the beam in your calculation.)' (add); C-28's 'including the framing' rule (floor fills 2410-2416); a decimal load '0.5 klf not including beam weight' (already right, A2-beam-13).

clusters.title: A beam's end fixity or a partial-span load is not read, and the engine's default simple span is used silently (fixed-free, built into a wall, fixed at one end, fixed-pinned, both ends fixed, load over the left half)
clusters.root_cause: reader.js beamAnalysisFields (2172-2179) sets support only from /\bcantilever(?:ed)?\b/ or 'simply supported|simple span|simple beam'. Anything else leaves the support box empty, and the frozen engine form beam_analysis takes its default 'simple' silently, with no ask (wL^2/8 = 14.5 where the cantilever's wL^2/2 = 58 is right, 4x too small). The finder-data 'other-beams' not-in-tool signals are literal phrases ('fixed at both ends', 'fixed-fixed beam', 'propped' ...), so 'both ends fixed' and 'fixed at one end and pinned at the other' get through. uniformLoads()/beamAnalysisFields place every klf load on the whole span, and no word for a partial load ('over the left half') is checked. The holdout H11 ('fixed support at the left end and free at the right end') prints the same wrong 14.5 for the same reason. In the corpus, 'fixed' in a beam question appears only as fixity wording.
clusters.fix_plan: reader.js beamAnalysisFields, right after the cant test (or a helper in a new file called from there; it also runs for beam_select's analysis object, hoist=false). (a) CANTILEVER (ANSWER) when no 'cantilever' word is present but the words say one end is fixed or built in and the other is free: '\bfixed[- ]free\b|\bfree[- ]fixed\b|\b(?:fixed|built[- ]?in(?:to)?|clamped)\b[^.;]{0,50}\bfree\b|\bfree\b[^.;]{0,50}\b(?:fixed|built[- ]?in|wall)\b|\b(?:sticks?|projects?|juts?)\s+out\s+(?:from|of)\s+(?:the\s+|a\s+)?wall', with no pinned|hinged|roller|propped|simply|simple|'both ends'|'at both' in the text. Then support = cantilever: 58 kip-ft for 182/183/184/196 and H11 (the page's own cantilever path already gives 58, A2-beam-163..165). (b) STOP, kind 'stop', one sentence with no number ('NOT answered here: this page works out simple spans and cantilevers only; if the other end is free, type the word cantilever'), for any other fixity word in a beam part: \bfixed\b|\bbuilt[- ]?in(?:to)?\b|\bclamped\b|\bencastr|\bpropped\b|\brestrained\s+against\s+rotation. This covers 'fixed at one end' or 'built into a wall at one end' with the other end not stated (144, 153: two readings, so never choose), fixed-pinned (185, 227) and 'both ends fixed' (186). (c) The same STOP for a uniform load on part of the span: '\bover\s+(?:the\s+)?(?:left|right|middle|central|cent(?:er|re)|first|last|end)\s+(?:half|third|quarter|portion|part|\d)|\bover\s+(?:one\s+|a\s+|the\s+)?(?:half|third|quarter|portion|part)\s+of\b|\bpartial(?:ly)?\s+(?:span|uniform|distributed|loaded|load)|\bfrom\s+x\s*=' (64). MUST NOT CHANGE: 'cantilever' in any spelling the spelling map fixes, including point loads measured 'from the free end/wall'; 'simply supported' / 'simple span'; beams 'supported on (masonry) walls' or a 'bearing wall' (no fixity word); 'fully braced' and 'braced' (not fixity); 'over the entire/full/whole span or length'; the finder's other-beams refusals (A2-beam-39, A2-beam-210). Run regress.sh and read every changed beam line.

clusters.title: A length written in feet and inches (20'-6", 8 ft 6 in) keeps only the feet in span, length and spacing
clusters.root_cause: reader.js findLengths (1284-1370). Every one-length rule builds its item through mk() from the feet number only: span 1318, 'N-ft span' 1325, 'span is' 1328, length/height 1332, spacing 1345/1348/1350. The ft-in regex at 1294 stores the full value in L.combos, but combos are used only when no span at all was read (beamAnalysisFields 2170). They are never used for spacing (floorBits) or by beam_max_live_load (2315 takes span || length). So 20'-6" becomes 20 ft, and 'spaced 8 ft 6 in' becomes 8 ft. The leftover '6 in' is hidden from the unplaced-number gate whenever another field quotes the same digit ('6 in slab').
clusters.fix_plan: One post-pass at the end of findLengths (reader.js). For L.span, L.length and L.spacing in ft: if a combo starts inside the item's match and ends after it (the inches follow the feet directly) and its inch part is < 12, replace the item with the combo (value ft + in/12, 'from' running through the inches, rule 'ft-in'). If the inches are directly followed by a thickness or size noun (thick|slab|deck|concrete|plate|bolt|dia|hole|deep|depth|wide|flange|web|leg), as in his comma-less 'spaced 8 ft 6 in slab', there are two readings: do not choose, ASK kind 'need' on that length. I prototyped this on a scratch copy and ran all 4,718 corpus questions: 16 change, every one to the right value (181: 243.75; 67: 209.4; loads-08: 1.445; also A2-beam-215/216/217/43 and loads-p40/58/59/76/78/79/80/81/82/165, where three refusals now answer 1.3175) and nothing regresses. MUST NOT CHANGE: 'L = 18 ft 6 in' (the labelled rule already adds the inches); '3 spaces of 6 ft 8 in'; a span given in inches ('246 in', already right); '6 in slab' as the slab thickness; column lengths given with labels.

clusters.title: In loads_factored and the beam fills, one load kind is missing, doubled, mixed in unit, or bound to the wrong number, and the 'factored' / 'service' basis that was read never holds the answer
clusters.root_cause: (i) The findLoads word rule (reader.js 267-270) has the gap [^0-9.;=]{0,28}?, which lets a label with no number of its own ('no dead load,', 'dead load is negligible,', 'no live load,') take the next load's number. The 2 klf is then used as both dead and live load (187/129/188). (ii) FILL.loads_factored (2505-2516) keeps the first D and the first L, takes the unit of the first load, and asks only when NEITHER kind was read. It computes loadBasis() at 2508 and never uses it. So: 'L = 2D', 'D = L = 20 k' and 'dead and live loads 20 k each' silently drop one kind (03, 04). A second dead load with the same value is hidden, because the unit field quotes the same words (05). plf is mixed with k/ft (07). 'factored dead load D = 30 k' has two readings (01), and 'service load D, L' asks for D + L (02), yet both still print 1.2D + 1.6L. (iii) The findLoads symbol rule at 236 reads 'Pu = 1.2D + 1.6L' as Pu = 1: N backtracks from 1.2 to 1, and '.' then passes the (?![A-Za-z0-9]) lookahead (06). (iv) beamAnalysisFields 2186-2189 raises loads_basis as a 'choice' on boxes it has already filled. mergeBoxes only attaches that as a ruleQuestion, and markReaderStops ignores it, so the factored loads are factored again (65). loadBasis 1426 needs a digit right after 'factored loads:', so 'factored loads: wD = 1.2' is read as service-symbol (150).
clusters.fix_plan: Same lane as L2 (load-pair-half-missing + load-number-misbound): extend those hunks, do not build a second load reader. (1) Put L2's half-missing ask (kind 'need') into FILL.loads_factored as well (after 2513) and into beamAnalysisFields for wD/wL (after 2185). Skip it when the missing kind is negated in its own clause (no|zero|none|negligible|neglect(ed)|= 0); then the box stays empty, which is right. With L2(c)'s gap fix this gives ANSWER 160 (187, 129) and 120 (188, with fix-hercombo). (2) L2(3)'s coverage patterns must also accept the no-verb form 'dead and live loads 20 k each' and 'D = L = 20 k' (04: 56). 'L = 2D', 'D = L', 'half the live load', 'L/D = 3' are relations: ASK. fix-hercombo already stops 03 itself, but not its D = L / L = 30 k, D = L variants. (3) FILL.loads_factored: two loads of the same kind at different positions (compare by index, not by value) raise an ASK, kind 'need', on D (or L) asking for the total; never keep the first silently (05). When d.unit and l.unit differ: klf with plf, convert plf/1000 and print k/ft (ANSWER 2.72 for 07); kips with lb, or psf with k/ft, ASK. (4) Use the computed basis. basis 'factored' from the words 'factored dead|live load' with no u-load: ASK, kind 'need' (01: a given factored value, or the asked 1.2D). Explicit service|working|unfactored, with the words never saying factored/Pu/wu/U: STOP in one sentence, no number ('the page works out factored loads; your question asks for the service load') (02). (5) L2(a): the unitless branch at 236 must reject the WHOLE numeric token when it is followed by a letter or '(': test the text after the full token for ^[\d.]*\s*[A-Za-z(*+]. L2's planned \s*[(*x+] misses '1.2D' because N backtracks to '1'. 06 then reads D = 20, L = 30 and prints 72. (6) beamAnalysisFields 2189: when the loads are said to be factored, do not fill wD/wL. If both are individually labelled factored (findLoads basis 'factored'), set already_factored and w_u = X + Y (ANSWER 220 for 65; the sum of two factored loads is wu, unambiguous). Otherwise ASK, kind 'need', on w_u. loadBasis givenFactored should also match 'factored\s+loads?\s*[:,]?\s*[A-Za-z]{1,3}\s*=' (L2(f), add ':'), so 150 asks. MUST NOT CHANGE: L2's list; 'dead load = 0' and 'dead load neglected' after the live load (already right); dead-load-only questions with no live word (hercombo/dcauses); the 'dead + live = 120 psf is a sum' guard; a given 'Pu = 800 kips'; C-28's framing weight.
clusters.overlaps: L2 load-reading ([load-pair-half-missing], [load-number-misbound] a/c/f); fix-hercombo (stops A2-loads-03 itself; 1.4D in A2-beam-188)

clusters.title: With no blank, a sentence asks for a different moment or load than the form prints (nominal Mn, plastic Mp, extra moment, unfactored or dead-load moment, ML, the moment at a point, a named 1.4D, the total load on a beam, wu in plf / as a line load), and the form's Mu / phi Mp / U stays a clean ANSWER
clusters.root_cause: pipeline.js ASK_WORDS / askedInWords (975-1035) know only the forms' main quantities. The qualifiers that change the quantity exist only on the blank path (wordId 922). 'nominal moment strength' matches phimn (989), the form's own result, so nothing is flagged. 'plastic moment', 'moment at the quarter point', 'moment due to dead load only' and 'ML' match nothing. 'unfactored moment' fails the mu entry, because 'unfactored' has no word boundary before 'factored'. asksInProse (1002) does not count 'how much' as asking. 'what is Mu for the load combination 1.4D' asks mu and gets the 1.2D + 1.6L carry (the chain's combo_first, ~3245). 'total factored load on the beam (in kips)' matches pu (993), which FORM_GIVES.floor_plan (817) claims to give, so the beam reaction stands as the answer. The asked unit is never compared with the printed one: SIG_VALUE.wu accepts loads_combinations' U_max in psf (loads-09: 32 psf printed for a k/ft line load), and a prose 'wu in plf' never reaches sigValueFor's klf-to-plf conversion (1240; the writeBlock unit check at 3809-3814 covers only kip-in vs kip-ft).
clusters.fix_plan: Build on L3's prose-ask helper (a new file called at the end of askedInWords); do not build a second one. Add to its qualifier list, for moments and loads: (a) 'nominal (moment|flexural) strength', \bMn\b(?!\s*=), 'plastic moment', \bMp\b(?!\s*=) with no phi give id 'mp' (it already exists on the blank route, in sigGives): ANSWER Mp = Fy Zx/12, 558.33 (106) and 138.33 (107). That is unambiguous for her fully braced beams. Exclude 'nominal' before the phimn match. (b) extra|additional|excess|reserve|spare|remaining + moment|capacity|load, with 'how much' counted as asking: UNKNOWN ask, so CHECK YOUR BLANK stands under the ANSWER (110). (c) unfactored|service|working + moment|load, 'moment due to (the) dead|live load (only)', \bM[DL]\b: UNKNOWN ask, CHECK (189, 131, 133). Also fix the mu entry so 'unfactored' never counts as 'factored'. (d) 'moment at <position>' where the position is not midspan, center or 'maximum' (quarter point, 'N ft from', x = N with N not L/2): UNKNOWN ask, CHECK (128, 125). (e) A load combination named in the asking sentence other than 1.2D + 1.6L ('1.4D', '0.9D', 'combination 1') gives a STOP in one sentence with no number: her class uses one combination (127). Coordinate with fix-hercombo. (f) 'total (factored) load on the beam|girder|joist' or 'W = wu L' is not pu (pu stays for column/axial/'on the column'): an UNKNOWN ask, so floor_plan's reaction line is no longer clean (loads-12). (g) Asked unit: when the asking sentence names a unit (in plf|lb/ft|klf|k/ft|kips|psf), compare its dimension with the printed value. Same dimension, other scale (plf vs k/ft): write the existing sigValueFor conversion as an 'ANSWER TO "wu in plf"' line with one number and demote the main line to ALSO FOUND (loads-14). A wu / 'line load' ask, or a spacing/tributary in the words, answered by a psf U_max: askedMismatch, the existing NOT WHAT YOUR BLANK ASKS line or a STOP (loads-09). Routing roof live as L to loads_floor (her rule) is optional coverage, only after regress. MUST NOT CHANGE: L3's list; 'find Mu', 'maximum moment', 'design moment strength phi Mn' (the form's own result); 'moment at midspan' of a simple uniform beam (= Mmax); the whole blank path; 'factored load on the column' = pu; word questions and multiple choice (C-48); the one-number ANSWER line (altnum).
clusters.overlaps: L3 prose-asks ([prose-ask-qualifier]); fix-hercombo (named 1.4D in A2-beam-127); fix-altnum (one number per ANSWER line)

clusters.title: A positive phrase is matched inside its own negation or neglect instruction: 'not a W16', 'not an interior/edge beam', 'not braced against sidesway', 'neglect shear lag'
clusters.root_cause: Each reader rule matches a positive phrase with no look at the words in front of it. FILL.beam_select 2284: a single W family named sets allowed_depths = [that depth], even after 'not a', 'except', 'other than', 'do not use' (the excluded W16X40 / W18X40 is printed). floorBits 2387/2388: the edge/inter regexes match inside 'is not an interior beam' / 'not an edge beam', so the tributary width is wrong by 2x. maySway 343-349: line 344 deletes 'braced against sidesway' out of 'not braced against sidesway', so the final \bnot\s+braced\s+against\b test can never match; the braced K 0.65 is used (599 printed for 293). tensionCommon (~1690-1736) has no rule for 'neglect / ignore / no shear lag', so Table D3.1's U = 0.90 is used (596.2 for 662.4).
clusters.fix_plan: reader.js, four local hunks. (1) beam_select 2284: test the 25 characters before the family for (?:\bnot|\bexcept|other\s+than|\bbut\s+not|\bexcluding|do\s+not\s+use|don't\s+use|\bavoid)\s+(?:an?\s+|the\s+)?$ (a slice test; ES5 has no lookbehind). When it is negated, allowed_depths = the nominal W depths list (as in the nominal-depth rule just below) minus that depth, with the rule text 'every W family but W16': ANSWER W18X40 (134) and W21X44 (152). (2) floorBits: a position phrase with not / isn't / no in the 20 characters before it is not a position word. The existing position ask then runs (it blocks on floor_plan: 'Beam position is required') and offers interior / edge / custom. ASK, because 'not interior' may be edge or a custom width (10, 11). (3) maySway: first .replace(/\b(?:not|never)\s+braced\s+against\s+(?:side[\s-]?)?sway\b/gi, ' unbraced against ') before line 344's deletion. 143 then gives ANSWER 293 (the page's own 'sidesway not prevented' route), and variant 171 (fixed-pinned, K 2.1) refuses on KL/r > 200; I checked that on the branch. (4) tensionCommon: '\b(?:neglect|ignore|disregard)\w*\s+(?:the\s+)?(?:effects?\s+of\s+)?shear\s+lag\b|\b(?:assume\s+)?no\s+shear\s+lag\b|\bshear\s+lag\s+(?:may|can|is\s+to|should)\s+be\s+(?:neglected|ignored)\b' sets U = 1.0 as given (like uStated): ANSWER 662.4 (149), and Ae 13.59 for the Ae variant. MUST NOT CHANGE: 'must be a W16', 'W16 only', 'lightest W16'; 'is an interior beam', 'edge beam', a beam with no position word (asks); 'braced against sidesway', 'sidesway prevented', 'unbraced frame'; 'use Table D3.1', 'find U', '(u=1)', and the cover-U exclusion at 1722 (a question that names shear lag).

clusters.title: The steel or bolt of something else becomes the member's: A36 gusset/end plates, 'not a36', the cover's 'A36 for plates', an inline default bolt; a short defaults line is read as the question's own words, and a long one drops its U
clusters.root_cause: reader.js findGrade (1252-1270) loops GRADES with A36 FIRST and keeps the first grade found anywhere (pickMatch falls back to any match). So the steel of gusset, end or base plates, 'not a36', 'instead of a36' and the cover's 'A36 for plates' all become the member's steel, and two grades are never treated as a conflict. Cover and defaults: splitPreamble (484) makes a cover line preamble only when it is > 80 characters, so a short defaults line is read as the question's own words (193: A36; 196: Fy 50 from the cover mixed with Fu 58 from the plates' A36). parseDefaults (491-502) understands neither a bare 'U = 1.0' nor 'A36 for plates', 'A992', 'Fu =' or 'N in bolts', so a long line silently drops the cover's U. The documented cover-U rule (1722) then never applies (197). pipeline.js coverLines (571) takes a one-line question that starts with 'unless noted' as cover AND keeps it as the question, so ctx holds it twice (145). findBolt (1214) returns the first diameter in the text, so an inline default '3/4 in bolts' beats the question's own '7/8 in bolts' (155).
clusters.fix_plan: Mostly reader.js. (1) findGrade: collect every grade match, in text order. Drop a grade with a negation or replacement before it (not|no|instead of|rather than|other than|except, ~20 chars). When the member is not a plate or bar, also drop a grade tied to a connection element: 'for plates', 'gusset', '(end|base|splice|connection) plates?', or 'plates? (are|is|of)' within ~25 characters. If one grade is left, use it (153: A572 gives 180; 174/145: A992 gives 359.2). If none is left, leave the grade null so the family default from her slide applies (W = A992), as today: 193 gives 502. If two different grades are left, ASK kind 'need' on Fy ('which steel is the member?'); never take the first. (2) splitPreamble: drop the length > 80 test for a line that starts with the cover marker and is not the last line; the 'last line is never preamble' rule stays. parseDefaults learns a bare \bU\s*=\s*(\d*\.?\d+), 'Fu = N ksi', 'A992' (rolled shapes), 'A36 for plates' (plates only) and 'N in bolts'. Each reader uses a default only when the question itself gives none. 196 and 197 then give 662.4 by the documented cover-U rule. (3) pipeline coverLines: a cover-marker line that is the only (or the last) line is the question, not cover, mirroring splitPreamble; a one-line hunk (145). (4) findBolt: gather every bolt diameter (kind 'bolt'). With two different sizes, the one outside a cover clause ('unless noted', 'assume', 'use ... unless') wins (155: 7/8 in gives 583.5); otherwise ASK kind 'need' on bolt_dia. MUST NOT CHANGE: a single grade anywhere in the text (the stem's grade reaching later parts through pickMatch); plate members 'PL ... A36'; 'A36 steel' columns where A36 really is the member; the loose 'Fy 36' and 'grade 50' forms; long cover lines typed in the defaults box (her Q23 'K = 1.0 for all columns', 'pinned support conditions', the loads-basis line); the 1722 cover-U exclusions.

clusters.title: Numbered problems on one line are not split, a later numbered part borrows an earlier column's length, and a leading problem number is read as a count
clusters.root_cause: (i) A second numbered problem on the same line ('... find phi pn. 2. a pl 1/2x8 ...', 'q1 ... q2 ...') is not split. pipeline.js splitAsks (646-671) counts an ask only when its verb opens a clause (ASK_VERB_RE 592), and the frozen finder does not take a mid-line '2.' or 'q2' as a part marker. The single part then mixes both problems: tensionCommon (reader 1582) takes the W as the member and ignores the PL (702), and findGrade takes q2's a36 for q1's column (368.6). (ii) carryAcross section 3 (pipeline ~3483) fills a later part's empty lengths, ends and Fy from an earlier column part, even when the later part names a DIFFERENT shape and says nothing like 'repeat' or 'same'. 471 is printed for a W10x49 whose length is not given, and the block does not say the length was borrowed. (iii) reader.js cgTokens (854/863): a leading 'N.' followed by a lower-case word is not a STOP or a label, so in '5. bolts per line: 3' the 5 becomes the count and the 'count LAST' rule never reads ': 3'.
clusters.fix_plan: (1) pipeline (a new file, or splitAsks): when the finder made ONE part of a text that has a problem marker after a sentence end or at a clause start, (?:^|[.?!;]\s*)(?:q\s?\d{1,2}\b|problem\s+\d+\b|\d{1,2}\s*[.)]\s+), and its own member shape on each side (two different members), STOP in one sentence with no number: 'Your text holds two numbered problems; type them one at a time.' (67, 147). Real splitting is optional coverage, after regress. (2) carryAcross section 3: skip the carry when the target part names a shape that differs from the source part's shape, unless the part says repeat|same|again|also|as in. Its length box then stays empty and required, so the page asks (146: ASK). (3) cgTokens: an integer at the start of the text or after a sentence end, followed by '.' or ')' and a space, is a label when the count phrase it would fill gets its own number after ':' or '='. That gives ANSWER 96.9 for 148 (596.2 / 129.6 for its variants). When no other number fills that count, go through the existing count_ conflict ask ('can be read two ways'); never use the label as a count (variant 216). MUST NOT CHANGE: lettered (a)/(b) parts and their carry from the stem; 'repeat (a) for a W10x49' (REF_RE); 'q4.', '4)', 'problem 4.', '4. given:' (already right); his own '(a) ... (b)' sample; a plain '3 bolts per line'.
clusters.overlaps: L3 stated-conditions [stated-condition-dropped](c) changes the same carryAcross section 3 (no carry into a part with its own unplaced length): one hunk for both

clusters.title: Column bracing: 'unbraced' / 'no bracing at mid height' read as a brace, a brace about the x axis put on y, and a brace sentence with no location ignored
clusters.root_cause: reader.js findBracing (1844-1856). Line 1846 has no \b before 'braced', so 'unbraced at mid height' matches, and no negation check ('no bracing at mid height', 'bracing at mid height: none', 'the brace ... has been removed'). It records no axis ('about the x axis', 'strong axis only'), and fillColumn (1943-1952) always puts the fraction on Ly. A brace statement with no location word ('(c) what if braced about both axes') is not read as a brace at all (it needs mid/third/quarter). bothDir needs Ls.brace.fraction, the stem's 20 ft fills both lengths, and (c) silently prints (a)'s 399 again.
clusters.fix_plan: Same lane as L2 [column-bracing-reading] (a) negation and (b) axis; do not plan it twice. Additions for that lane: a \b before 'braced' and the 'un' prefix (15: 399); a negation AFTER the match counts too (': none', 'none', 'is not provided'; variant 163); the axis words 'x axis', 'x-x', 'strong axis', 'strong direction' and 'weak axis is not' (151: 399.2). New: a brace statement with no location word (braced about or in both axes/directions, braced about the weak axis), in a part whose own text gives no mid/third/quarter/height, raises an ASK kind 'need' on Ly/Lx ('where along the column is the brace?'). Never the unbraced answer (140 (c)). MUST NOT CHANGE: L2's list (plain 'braced at mid-height', 'in both directions', 'braced against sidesway', HW 5-17 segments, the 9/9 third-point column).

clusters.root_cause: The floorsN regex (reader.js 747-753) needs '<n>\s+(floor|story|storey)', so 'three levels', '4-story' and 'four-story' are not read. FILL.loads_takedown 2482 asks for 'floors' with no kind, so the frozen engine default 0 goes in (pipeline mergeBoxes 549, state 'default'). The page prints the roof alone, 22.4 for 233.6, as a clean ANSWER; only the read box says the floor loads were not used.
clusters.fix_plan: Same lane as L2 [takedown-floors-and-levels] (a)/(b); do not plan twice. Additions: (1) Safety: line 2482 asks with kind 'need' whenever floor loads (floor_D_psf / floor_L_psf) were read. Never the default 0 with floor loads in the words; this also covers a text with no count at all (ASK). (2) Coverage: the count regex also accepts a hyphen ('4-story', 'four-story'), and '(the )?roof and (WN) (levels|floors)' gives floors = N below the roof. That is unambiguous: ANSWER 233.6. A bare 'N levels' or 'N-story building' with roof loads keeps L2(b)'s ASK. MUST NOT CHANGE: L2's list; a roof-only column ('supports only the roof') stays at 0 floors with no ask.

clusters.title: A NEGATED bracing phrase ('not braced against sidesway', 'not a braced frame', 'isnt braced against sway', 'the building has no bracing') is read as BRACED, and fixed-fixed / fixed-pinned keep the braced K (0.65 / 0.8)
clusters.root_cause: reader.js maySway() (l.342-350). Its first .replace (l.344) deletes 'braced against (side)sway' from inside 'not braced against sidesway' and leaves a bare 'not'. So the final test's /\bnot\s+braced\s+against\b/ (l.349) can never match. The same happens to 'not a braced frame' (l.348 removes 'braced frame') and to 'isnt braced against sway'. 'no bracing' (the building / frame has no bracing) is not a sway phrase at all. maySway returns false, so findEnds l.463-464 keeps fixed-fixed (K 0.65, also printed through column_capacity: 1100 kips where 929 is right) or fixed-pinned (K 0.8). I re-ran all six on branch cloud: they reproduce. The corpus has the same misses (k04, k16, k24, k25, k26, k28, z07, z15, A2-noise-60). A bare 'not braced' with no 'against' (k03, k11 'fixed at the base and pinned at the top, not braced') also prints 0.8 clean.
clusters.fix_plan: reader.js only, inside maySway plus one line in findEnds. (1) At the TOP of maySway, before any .replace, return true when the RAW text has a negated sway-bracing phrase: /\b(?:not|never|isn'?t|is\s*nt|aren'?t|wasn'?t)\s+(?:a\s+|an\s+)?braced\s+(?:against\s+(?:side[\s-]?)?sway|against\s+(?:lateral\s+)?translation|frame)\b|\b(?:frame|building|structure)\s+(?:is\s+not|isn'?t|is\s*nt)\s+braced\b|\b(?:frame|building|structure)\s+(?:has|have|with)\s+no\s+(?:lateral\s+|sway\s+)?bracing\b|\bno\s+bracing\s+against\s+(?:side[\s-]?)?sway\b/i. Write the comment with case A2-look-01 / k28. The existing l.463 rule then turns fixed-fixed into fixed-sway, so ANSWER K = 1.2 and column phi Pn = 929 (look-01/02/03/04/06). l.464 drops fixed-pinned, so look-05 ASKs the end conditions, which is right because 'pinned top free to sway' has two readings. (2) Optional, same file: a new swayUnclear(t) for a BARE 'not braced' / 'unbraced' / 'no bracing' NOT followed in its clause by at|about|along|in the (weak|strong|x|y)|mid|between|over|for|in either direction. In findEnds, a braced reading (pinned-pinned, fixed-fixed, fixed-pinned) with swayUnclear true becomes r = [], which is an ASK, never a conversion to 1.2 (k03/k11). MUST NOT CHANGE: 'braced against sidesway' (no negation), 'braced frame', 'non-sway', 'sidesway prevented', 'not braced at mid height', 'no bracing at mid-height', 'no bracing about the weak axis', 'not braced in either direction' (A1-ccap-24/54/55/101/103, A2-noise-14/15/121/141), 'unbraced length', and the noMove regex (l.422). Run harness/regress.sh and read every K / column change.

clusters.title: A steel grade typed with a product or shape (A36 angle, A572 Gr 50 plate, A500 Gr B HSS, 'gr 50', A53 pipe) is ignored: the product's slide default or the form's Fy = 50 is printed
clusters.root_cause: Four places. (a) reader.js FILL.lookup_material (l.2551-2554) fills 'what' from the shape (high) or a product word (medium) and never reads a typed grade. pipeline.js markGrade (l.2949-2953) reads a grade only when that box is EMPTY, so the product or shape default wins (look-07..12). The corpus shows the same misses: m08, g06, g07, g08, g10, g11, g09. (b) expand.js chunksOf (l.233-243) cuts at ',' and parseMat (l.297-327) makes 'plate, A572 Gr. 50' / 'L4x4x1/2 ,A36' into TWO items: (a) the product default, clean, and (b) the grade (look-13/14). (c) FILL.lookup_critical_stress (l.2022-2026) calls fillFy (l.1476), which reads only a typed Fy or a GRADES row (l.1233). GRADES has no A53 / A500 row, product words (pipe, plate, HSS) are never consulted, and 'grade B' is not read. So the form's Fy 50 is used silently (look-15..18). (d) findGrade (l.1255) takes the FIRST 'Fy = n ksi'. A second, different Fy never stops (look-19). 'gr 50' with no A-number is read by nothing (look-12). The engine refuses 'A500 Grade B' (not on her slide), so the existing markGrade path cannot answer look-11 either.
clusters.fix_plan: reader.js + expand.js. No pipeline change. (1) FILL.lookup_material: collect the typed grades with markGrade's regex, extended to A53/A500 and 'Gr B/C'. Keep only distinct grades and the part's own text. Exactly one grade ON HER SLIDE (A36, A992, A572 [Gr 50], A53 [Gr B], A500 [Gr C]): B.set('what', canonical grade, m[0], 'high', 'the steel your question names'). ANSWER: look-07 36/58, look-08 36, look-09 50/65, look-10 Fu 58, g06 50/62, g07 36/58. A grade NOT on her slide (A500 Gr B, A572 Gr 42/55/60/65, A588, A242, A913, A529): B.ask(..., 'stop') with one sentence and no number ('Your question names a steel that is not on her steel slide; the page does not look it up. NOT answered here.'), so look-11 STOPs. Two different grades in one item: ASK which (need). A bare 'gr/grade NN' with no A-number, where NN differs from the product default Fy: STOP/ASK for the ASTM name (look-12). Never the A36 default. (2) expand.js parseMat: exactly two chunks, one holding only a shape/product and the next holding only a grade, separated by a comma (his ' ,A36'): return null, so the single reader takes it as ONE item (look-13/14 give 50/65 and 36/58). Keep the split for 'and'/'or' lists (g16). (3) FILL.lookup_critical_stress: after fillFy, if no Fy was read: (i) add GRADES rows A53 [Gr B] 35/60 and A500 [Gr C] 50/62 (reader table, not frozen data) and ANSWER look-16 (21.8). (ii) A typed A-grade that GRADES lacks (A500 Gr B) gives a STOP (look-18). (iii) With no grade, a product word gives her slide's steel (pipe 35, plate 36; HSS/angle/W stay 50) with confidence medium and a note 'her slide: <product> steel'. ANSWER look-15 21.8 and look-17 22.1, the same steel column_capacity already uses for a Pipe. (4) findGrade: record the distinct 'Fy = n' values of the part's own text. fillFy raises B.ask('fy_two', 'Two yield stresses are given. Which one is the member's?', ['Fy'], values, 'need') when there are two or more (look-19, x12). MUST NOT CHANGE: BL-023 family (A36 gusset plate), BL-025 family (A53 Gr B Pipe 6 STD), g15 'A36 plate', g16 list, 'Fy of a W14x90' (A992), 'gra de b' typing, typed 'Fy = 36 ksi' in calculation forms, and the f07 'phi Fcr ... A36' path. Run regress.sh: (4) touches every form, so classify each change.

clusters.title: A sentence that asks for the NOMINAL value (Fcr, Pn, Mn, 'nominal axial strength', '(not phi Pn)') or the ASD value (Pn/omega, Fcr/omega, 'allowable strength') gets the form's phi (LRFD design) value as a clean ANSWER
clusters.root_cause: pipeline.js: the nominal conversion (SIG_NOMINAL l.846, sigValue l.1096) and the 'nominal|allowable|asd|omega' guard (wordId l.922) are reached only through askedBlanks, that is, a typed 'Sym = ____'. On the sentence path: asksInProse (l.1002) needs an asking verb, so a question typed as a bare head phrase ('Pn for a W10x49 ...', 'Fcr for KL/r = 85 ...', 'nominal axial strength of ...', 'allowable strength of ...') asks nothing. ASK_WORDS (l.975-999) has no bare Fcr / Pn / Mn / nominal entry, and its phipn / phifcr entries match 'phi Pn' inside '(not phi Pn)'. writeBlock's STRENGTH_ASK (l.1038) keeps the form's ANSWER whenever 'strength' is in the text. This is the same root as lane L3 prose-asks [prose-ask-qualifier]. That plan covers 'nominal' / bare 'Pn' -> pn and 'allowable|ASD|omega' -> STOP, but only for sentences its asking test accepts. It does not name Fcr, Mn/Mp, '(not phi X)', or verb-less head phrases that contain digits.
clusters.fix_plan: Hand these 9 hits to the prose-asks fixer as extra test cases, plus this delta in the same new helper file. Do not add a second mechanism. (1) Asking test: the part's FIRST clause counts as asking even with digits and no verb when it STARTS with a quantity name followed by for|of ('Pn for a W10x49', 'Fcr for KL/r = 85', 'nominal axial strength of', 'allowable strength of', 'effective net area of'). (2) Before the ASK_WORDS phi entries match, strip '(not phi X)' / 'not phi X' / 'rather than phi X' / 'instead of phi X', and record that the sentence asks the NOMINAL X. (3) Map bare 'Fcr' (no phi in front), 'nominal (critical|buckling) stress' -> fcr; 'Mn', 'nominal moment (strength)' -> mn; 'Mp' / 'plastic moment' -> mp; bare 'Pn', 'nominal (axial|compressive) strength' -> pn. The existing SIG_NOMINAL / 'mp' sigValue then prints ANSWER TO '...': Fcr = 26.5/0.90 = 29.4 (look-20/21), Pn = 523 (look-22/23/24), Mp = Fy Zx/12 = 420.8 (look-25), and the phi line becomes ALSO FOUND. Unambiguous: one phi each. (4) 'omega' / '/ omega' / 'ASD' / 'allowable (strength|stress|load)' on column, Fcr or beam forms: one-sentence STOP with no number ('her class is LRFD; the page gives design values phi Pn, not ASD values. NOT answered here'). This covers look-26/27/28, which STRENGTH_ASK otherwise keeps clean. MUST NOT CHANGE: 'phi Fcr for KL/r = 85' and Table 4-14 lookups, 'design strength', 'available strength' (LRFD), her review 'Find: Euler Pcr, the AISC phi Pn', 'Pn = ____' blanks (already right), 'Fy = 50' given values, 'maximum allowable load' max-load questions (lane max-load-ask-unrouted owns them).
clusters.overlaps: prose-asks (lane L3, [prose-ask-qualifier]): same root (qualifier words read only on the blank path); this cluster adds Fcr/Mn/Mp, '(not phi X)', verb-less head phrases with digits, and omega/allowable on column and Fcr forms

clusters.title: A shape look-up answers the wrong property: a property typed WITH its value wins over the one asked, a ratio becomes one of its symbols (or two look-ups), 'nominal depth' becomes d, 'web and flange thickness' gives tf only, a single angle's minor axis becomes y, and '2 W14x90' prints the one-shape row
clusters.root_cause: reader.js findProperty (l.780-805) loops over PROPS (l.774-779, order tw, tf, bf, Z, S, r, I, d, A, W) and takes the FIRST entry that matches ANYWHERE. (a) A given 'tw=0.44 in', '(Zx = 157)', 'bf = 6.49', 'tf=.38in', 'depth 14 in', '(its tw is 0.44 in)' beats the asked radius of gyration, section modulus, moment of inertia, flange width or area (look-29..34). (b) No ratio is read: 'rx/ry', 'Zx/Sx', 'h/tw', 'flange width to thickness ratio', 'ratio of rx to ry' give the first symbol or name (look-35, 37-40), and expand.js chunksOf (l.236) cuts at '/' into two look-ups (look-36, 41). (c) PROPS maps '(actual|nominal) depth' to d (look-42). (d) 'web and flange thickness' does not match /web\s+(?:width|thickness)/, so tf wins, and expand leaves 'web' as residue (look-59). (e) Weak/minor maps to y for every family (l.793-794). For a single angle the minor principal axis is z, and the engine HAS rz/Iz/Sz (checked: L4X4X1/2 rz 0.776, L6X4X1/2 Iz 3.54) (look-43..45). (f) A count of shapes is never read: findProperty needs 'of a/an/the' (l.783), so '2 W14x90' prints the full one-shape row. markBuiltUp (pipeline l.2793) covers only section_properties/column forms (look-60; also 'two C10x30 back to back' prints the C10X30 row).
clusters.fix_plan: reader.js findProperty / FILL.lookup_shape + expand.js parseShape. (a) First, because it is the likely one (he types table values along): in the PROPS loop and in the sym rule, SKIP a match that is followed by a value (^\s*(?:=|:|is|of)?\s*\.?\d) and continue with the next entry. ANSWER: look-29 ry 3.70, 30 Sx 143, 31 Ix 204, 32 bf 6.49, 33 A 26.5, 34 Ix 999. If every property word is a given, keep today's behaviour. (b) Ratios: 'bf/2tf', 'flange (width-to-thickness|slenderness)' -> property 'bf/2tf'; 'h/tw', 'web (width-to-thickness|slenderness)' -> 'h/tw'. Both are rows of the frozen data and the engine answers them, so ANSWER 10.2 and 25.9. Any other ratio (two property symbols joined by '/', 'ratio of X to Y', 'X to Y ratio', 'shape factor') gives a STOP with no number ('a ratio of two properties is not looked up here'). expand.js parseShape returns null for the same texts, so it never splits a ratio (look-36/41). (c) 'nominal depth': STOP ('the nominal depth is the number in the shape's name; the page gives the actual depth d'). expand already declines it. (d) expand.js PW: add '(?:web\s+and\s+flange|flange\s+and\s+web)\s+thickness(?:es)?' -> two elements tw, tf, so it gives two look-ups, as 'tw and tf of' already does (ANSWER 0.345 and 0.575). (e) A single angle (kind L, not 2L) with weak|minor|z words: equal legs -> axis z (ANSWER rz 0.776 for look-43/44). Unequal legs -> ASK geometric y or principal z (look-45), because some books mean Iy. expand parseShape returns null for an L with a weak/minor axis word. (f) FILL.lookup_shape: a count (2-9, two..four, pair of, double, twin) right before a non-L shape name, a word count before an L name that findShapes did not read as 2L, or 'back to back' / 'side by side' / 'built-up' with one shape name gives a STOP with no number ('more than one shape: this look-up gives one rolled shape only'). MUST NOT CHANGE: 'Ix of W14x90', 'A of a WT12X88', 'tdes of HSS...', 'tw and tf of a w12x53' (two parts), 2L names, W/C weak axis = y, 'radius of gyration about the weak axis of a W14x90' = ry.

clusters.title: His space before a slash ('L6x6x1 /2', 'L6 x6 x1 /2') cuts the thickness to '1', and a REAL other angle (L6X6X1, L8X6X1, L8X8X1) is used silently, in look-ups AND calculations
clusters.root_cause: reader.js findShapes: FR (l.150) accepts 'd d/d', 'd/d', '.d' and 'd', but not 'd /d' or 'd/ d'. So the L regex (l.166; the same applies to 2L l.164, HSS l.168 and plates) ends the name at '1', and the leftover ' /2' is masked and never questioned. The shape exists, so nothing stops. I confirmed it reaches calculations on the branch: 'L6x6x1 /2 tension member welded find phi pn' prints phi Pn = 495 kips from L6X6X1 (Ag 11). HSS6x6x1 /2 and L4x4x1 /2 are refused only because those names do not exist. expand.js FRQ (l.62) has the same gap. His own typing model lists '3 /4' as normal.
clusters.fix_plan: reader.js (and expand.js FRQ for lists). (1) FR: add the alternatives '\\d+\\s+\\/\\s*\\d+|\\d+\\s*\\/\\s+\\d+' (a space on either side of the slash) after the mixed-number alternative, so 'x1 /2' reads 1/2. Edit with the Edit tool (backslashes). compactDim / legName must remove the inner spaces of the fraction before the name is built ('1 /2' -> '1/2'). (2) Safety net in findShapes: a shape match whose next characters are \\s*\\/\\s*\\d (a fraction left over) is not read. The part then STOPs/ASKs for the shape, instead of using a shorter real name. ANSWER: look-46 L6X6X1/2 A = 5.77, look-47 L8X6X1/2 A = 6.80, look-48 5.77, and the tension example uses Ag 5.77. MUST NOT CHANGE: 'L5x3-1/2x1/2' / 'L5 x 3 1/2 x 1/2' legs, 'L4x4x1/2, 3/4 in bolts' (a comma, not a slash), 'PL 1/2 x 10', '1 1/2' mixed numbers, 'W10/W12' families, the bolt '3 /4 in' reading. Run regress.sh and look at every shape-name change.

clusters.title: 'Standard hole' / 'per Table J3.3' / 'nominal diameter of a standard hole' is answered with her NET-AREA hole (bolt + 1/8)
clusters.root_cause: The frozen finder routes these to lookup_hole. reader.js FILL.lookup_hole (l.2555) reads only the bolt, and the engine's ANSWER is always 'Hole size for net area: bolt + 1/8'. The J3.3 standard hole appears only in the engine's step 2 text. No reader or pipeline guard reads 'standard' / 'J3.3' / 'nominal hole'. Only expand.js parseHole (l.357) declines them, and only for lists. The corpus has the same clean wrong line on q15, h02 and the whole BL-031 family (8 variants, 'According to Table J3.3 ... nominal diameter of a standard hole for a 3/4 in. bolt' -> 0.875 where 13/16 is right). Her rules.js ('standard = bolt + 1/16') and J3.3 (bolt + 1/8 from 1 in up) also disagree for 1 in bolts.
clusters.fix_plan: reader.js FILL.lookup_hole only (smallest safe). When the words ask the STANDARD hole itself: /\\bstandard\\s+hole|\\btable\\s+j\\s?3\\.?3\\b|\\bnominal\\s+(?:hole|diameter\\s+of\\s+(?:a|the)\\s+(?:standard\\s+)?hole)|\\bover-?sized?\\s+hole|\\bslot/i, with no 'net area|deduct|for computing|to subtract' in the same sentence. Then B.ask('std_hole', one sentence with no number, [], null, 'stop'): 'Your question asks the standard hole of the Specification's hole table; this page gives only the hole width her net-area rule deducts. NOT answered here.' No digits ('J3.3' has digits, so do not quote it). Optional later, only after the stop is in: a pipeline ANSWER TO line from the engine's step text 'Table J3.3 lists the standard hole itself as X in' (13/16, 15/16, 1-1/8), with the net-area line demoted to ALSO FOUND. Unambiguous per J3.3, but it needs a pipeline hunk. MUST NOT CHANGE: 'hole diameter for a 3/4in bolt' / 'hole size for net area' (bolt + 1/8, her rule: q14, a16, x01, x02, BL-030 family, BL-032, BL-043), 'standard holes' inside tension questions (k24 is tension_net_area, not lookup_hole), A2-words-39.

clusters.title: U from Table D3.1: '4 lines' is taken as 4 bolts per line (an invented second item printed clean), and 'through its web and flanges' is read as web only (case 7 instead of case 1)
clusters.root_cause: (a) expand.js parseU (l.397-407): COUNT_RE (l.393) takes any bare digit, and 'lines' is a filler in FILL_U (l.395). So in '3 bolts per line, 4 lines' the '4' becomes a second bolts-per-line count, and itemsOf writes part (b) 'with 4 bolts per line'. Part (a) refuses correctly, but part (b) prints U = 0.70 / 0.85 clean (look-52/53). '4 bolts per line, 2 lines' gives the same false split (b refused). (b) reader.js findHoles location regex (l.1192) captures only the FIRST element after 'through its' ('connected through its web'), so 'and flanges' sets no locFlange. tensionCommon (l.1712) then sets conn = 'web' (case 7, 0.70). The engine's 'all' (case 1, U = 1.0, checked) is never chosen (look-54).
clusters.fix_plan: (1) expand.js COUNT_RE: add a negative lookahead so a number followed by \\s+(?:gage\\s+)?(?:lines?|rows?) is not a count. The digit then stays in the residue, parseU returns null, and the single reader takes the question whole: look-52/53 STOP (3 per line in the web / 2 per line in the flanges is not case 7), and '4 bolts per line, 2 lines' ANSWERs 0.70 once. (2) reader.js findHoles, after the location loop: /(?:through|in|to|at)\\s+(?:its\\s+|the\\s+|both\\s+)?(?:web\\s+and\\s+(?:its\\s+|the\\s+|both\\s+)?flanges?|flanges?\\s+and\\s+(?:its\\s+|the\\s+)?web)\\b|\\ball\\s+(?:its\\s+)?(?:elements|parts)\\b/ sets both H.locWeb and H.locFlange. The existing 'hasF && hasW' branch then sets conn 'all', so ANSWER U = 1.0 (case 1, every element connected, her case 1). 'no holes/bolts in the web' must still win (noWeb), and so must lane L1's negation scoping. MUST NOT CHANGE: 'U for 3 and 4 bolts per line' lists, 'connected through the flanges only' / 'web only', case 7/8 values (0.90/0.85/0.70/0.80/0.60), her May 2024 Q8 'four lines ... through its flanges'.
clusters.overlaps: tension-geometry (lane L1) for A2-look-54 only: its (b) 'both legs = Case 1, U = 1.0' reads the same findHoles location words (one element captured); put the web+flanges pattern in the same hunk. A2-look-52/53 are expand.js only (no overlap).

clusters.root_cause: (a) pipeline.js askedLines l.1515 'v = sigValueFor(...); if (!v) continue;' silently drops an asked quantity that the form gives in general (sigGives > 0) but this run does not hold. In no-holes mode tension_capacity has no Ae value, so no line, no demotion and no warning appear. I checked on the branch: 'effective net area of a w14x90 Ae = ____ in2' prints the phi Pn ANSWER with nothing under it. The verb-less prose 'effective net area of a w14x90 no holes' is not even an ask (asksInProse needs a verb). (b) reader.js tensionCommon l.1649: the holes_count ask has the default kind 'value', which does not block, so tension_net_area runs with zero holes when the words name none ('net area of a w14x90' -> An = Ag). A count that is not in the words becomes 0. (c) The frozen finder routes 'area of a w14x90 minus two 1 in holes' to lookup_shape, and FILL.lookup_shape (l.2531) never looks at hole words.
clusters.fix_plan: (1) pipeline.js askedLines l.1515 (a 2-3 line hunk): when !v and sigGives(lastFn, b.id) > 0, set part.askedMissing = b. writeBlock then uses the EXISTING askedMismatch path: a 'NOT WHAT YOUR BLANK ASKS' line, and the ANSWER is demoted. For a typed blank, always. For a prose ask, only when it is the part's only ask. This must be the SAME hunk as lane L3 form-choice-guards (a), which handles 'gives none of the asks'; this is 'gives it in general, not in this run'. The verb-less head phrase comes from the prose-asks delta (cluster nominal-asd-sentence). (2) reader.js tensionCommon: for fn tension_net_area with NO hole/bolt/rivet/welded/'no holes' word, raise holes_count with kind 'need'. clusters.title: Multiple choice: the page CIRCLES a letter for a negated stem ('which is false', 'is NOT a', 'does NOT describe'), for a stem whose matched quote names ANOTHER choice, for an entry named by two symbols (Fcr and Fe), and for a capital G (gage vs shear modulus)
clusters.root_cause: pipeline.js SOLVE.choicePick (l.3662-3710). Route 1 (symbol, MC_SYMBOL_RE / MC_SYMBOL_END_RE l.3653-3654) and route 2 (definition) have NO negation test. contentWords (l.~3720) drops 'not' as a CHOICE_STOP word, so route 2 matches her positive sentence. wordsx choose() (l.691) does abstain on NEG_RE and on ties, but the merge at pipeline.js l.2028-2032 acts only when wordsx GIVES a letter, so the abstention never clears cur9.mc.best (242, 243, 244, 236). Route 2 circles the choice that fits the best entry's NAME even when that entry's quote names another choice as the thing described: PL quote -> 'modulus of elasticity' (245), 'Crushing vs buckling' -> 'elastic buckling' (237/230), 'Strain hardening' quote -> 'ultimate strength' (238; wordsx agrees, so no cross-check catches it), 'Plastic range' quote -> 'ductile' (228). Route 1 l.3677: 'last' = the last word of 'Critical stress Fcr and elastic buckling stress Fe', so a two-symbol entry counts as THE entry for Fe (246). The MULTI table (l.3685) has no G (gage / shear modulus), and the symbol match is case-sensitive, so 'G' in s^2/4G hits the shear modulus (161). With two choices, SOLVE.choiceCheck (l.3748, used at l.3805) prints 'Your choice: a' with no negation test (186).
clusters.fix_plan: pipeline.js small local hunks inside choicePick / choiceCheck. If the local builder is busy in pipeline.js, put them in a NEW file loaded after pipeline.js that wraps SOLVE.choicePick / SOLVE.choiceCheck (both are called through SOLVE). (1) Negation: route 1 gives no letter when the stem has not|false|incorrect|untrue|except|never|n't|isnt|doesnt (wordsx NEG_RE). Route 2 gives no letter when the stem has a negation word that the best entry's quotes do not also contain, because the route cannot see polarity. choiceCheck returns null on the same test (186). The existing 'NO LETTER FROM THE PAGE' line then prints. No inversion: never turn her sentence round. (2) Route 2: no letter when ANOTHER choice's content words (stemmed, all of them) appear in the best entry's quotes (245, 237, 230, 238, 228). (3) Route 1: skip an entry whose name, without brackets, holds ' and ' / ' vs ' / two symbol tokens (246). Add G: ['gage', 'shear modulus'] to MULTI (161). The existing mm > 1 rule then gives no letter. (4) Optional: at the l.2028 merge, a wordsx abstention whose noLetterWhy is the NOT/EXCEPT reason clears cur9.mc.best (belt and braces for (1)). Every case here becomes NO LETTER (zero wrong). Coverage of positive MCs is untouched. MUST NOT CHANGE: C-48 (multiple choice with word choices stays a word question), 'in which E is' with one modulus choice, symbol picks of single-symbol entries, positive definition picks whose quote names no other choice. A route-2 stem with 'without' / 'not' inside her own quote keeps its letter only when the quote has the same word. Run regress.sh and read every CIRCLE that disappears; a lost letter is acceptable, a new one is not.

clusters.title: Open word questions: the entry whose NAME is inside the question is printed as ANSWER even when a negation or split negative prefix stands in front of it ('dis advantages', 'un braced', 'in elastic', 'not ductile'), or when the question asks one item of a container entry, a symbol, a comparison, or a list
clusters.root_cause: The frozen engine lookup_definition matches the longest entry name contained in the query (values.matched_by = 'name_in_query', values.matched_name = e.g. 'ductile', 'advantages of steel', 'stress strain curve'). pipeline.js wordAnswer (l.3552-3590) keeps it as ANSWER when wordsx agrees (l.3562 'eng === first', mode keep) or has it anywhere in its top 3 (l.3566, the 'two readers' rule). Nothing checks (A) the words right in front of the matched name: a negation 'not/non/no' (145, 162, 167) or a negative prefix typed apart 'dis ', 'dis-', 'un ', 'in ' (190, 119, 201, 191, 52, 08). wordsx rank (l.449-458) also ignores the 2-letter prefix in its order-free name subset, so its top agrees, and for 07 wordsx.top itself is 'Disadvantages of a braced frame'. Nothing checks (B) whether the entry answers what is asked: the container synonym 'stress strain curve' of the points-list entry swallows every 'what is the X called' curve question (115, 60, 202, 63, 61, 11); the frozen PL synonym 'slope of the straight line' wins a near-tie, 47.54 vs 47.14 (65); 'what does S / Lr stand for' gets the load-combination entry that does not name the symbol (198, 116); wordsx ranks G first with its whole synonym in the question but the 'two readers' rule keeps E (142); a 'difference between X and Y' gets one entry's top (wordsx analyze l.880, 199); 'list 3 reasons' keeps the one-liner while wordsx ranks the list entry first (219). With the prefix rejoined, the engine answers correctly: checked 'disadvantages of steel', 'unbraced frame advantages', 'disadvantages of a moment frame', 'disadvantages of an unbraced frame', 'list two disadvantages of a braced frame'.
clusters.fix_plan: A small helper in wordsx.js or a NEW file, one hunk in wordAnswer, and the query rewrite in reader.js FILL.lookup_definition. (A1) Coverage: rejoin a split negative prefix ONLY when the joined word is one of hers: 'dis advantages' / 'dis-advantages' -> disadvantages, 'un braced' -> unbraced, 'un factored' -> unfactored, 'non sway' -> nonsway. Check with wordsx ownWord, never blindly: 'dis ign' (BC-090 = design) must not join. Apply it to the query in FILL.lookup_definition (l.2559) and to wordsx's query tokens. ANSWER with her Disadvantages / unbraced entries (190, 119, 201, 191, 07, 52). Do NOT rejoin 'in elastic', which has two readings. (A2) Guard in wordAnswer: when matched_by is 'name_in_query' and the 1-2 tokens before matched_name in the question are not|non|no|never|without|n't|isnt|arent or a lone dis|un|in|im|ir, give NO ANSWER. Print WARNING ('your words put NOT / a negative prefix in front of "<name>": her entry for it is the opposite; the page does not turn it round; if you meant one word, retype it') plus the existing 'HER SENTENCES ABOUT THIS -- the page does not choose' list (08, 145, 162, 167). (B) Asked-form guards in wordAnswer, each a demotion to the her-sentences list, never a new pick: (B1) the engine entry's definition is a ';'-list of 3+ items, and the question asks ONE thing ('is called', 'what is the (point|region|slope|area) ...', 'which point', 'what does ... represent'): 115, 60, 202, 63, 61, 11. (B2) a near tie: wordsx hits[1].score >= 0.97 x hits[0].score with a different entry (65). (B3) the 'two readers' rule (l.3566) keeps eng only when no OTHER entry's full name or synonym is in the question overlapping eng's matched name (142). (B4) 'what does X stand for / mean / represent' with a 1-3 letter symbol X: keep only an entry that names X as a symbol, else demote (198, 116). (B5) wordsx analyze: 'difference between A and B' / 'compare A and B' / 'A vs B' sets no top unless the entry's name holds both A and B (199). (B6) 'list|name|give N ...' with wordsx hits[0] a list entry different from eng: no keep (219). MUST NOT CHANGE: the mock 'why does the number of bolts in the line change the capacity?' (l.3566 keep, engine right, matcher third: (B3)/(B6) must not catch it), C-48, positive definitions ('a material that is brittle is called' -> Brittle), 'what is the advantage of an unbraced frame', 'inelastic buckling ...' typed as one word, 'non-interior' in calculation parts (A2-loads-p125: word parts only). Run regress.sh and read every word-part change; demotions are acceptable, new ANSWER lines need a check against her store.
